question: ***Which Dutch rock band*** reached number 7 in the UK singles chart in 1973 with the song ‘Radar Love’, which has since been covered more than 800 times, including by REM, U2, and Def Leppard?

Popular for its ability to be moulded and used widely for telephones, kitchenware, jewellery and toys, ***what polymer***, partly named for its developer, is formed from a condensation reaction of phenol with formaldehyde and is considered the first synthetic plastic?
***What is the second largest island*** in the Philippines by both area and population?
***Which sportswoman***, the daughter of Princess Anne, won the BBC Sports Personality of the Year award in 2006, after achieving individual gold in that year’s World Eventing Championships?

Released at the end of 2024, the film biopic A Complete Unknown stars Timothée Chalamet as ***which iconic American musician*** during his early career in the folk clubs of New York’s Greenwich Village in the early 1960s?

***What two-word alliterative term*** is used to refer collectively to the American liberal arts colleges Bryn Mawr, Barnard, Mount Holyoke, Smith, Wellesley, Radcliffe and Vassar, reflecting these colleges’ historical intake?

***What is the name of the edge jump*** in figure skating that is accomplished with a takeoff from the back inside edge of one foot and a landing on the back outside edge of the opposite foot? Quadruple versions of this jump are abbreviated 4S in scoring notation.

***Which organic redox reaction***, discovered by and named for a nineteenth-century Italian scientist, involves the disproportionation of non-enolizable aldehydes, resulting in the formation of an alcohol and a carboxylate salt?

Premiering on Paramount+ in November 2024, ***which US TV drama*** stars Michael Fassbender as ‘Martian’, a CIA operative based in London, and Richard Gere as his handler? It is an English-language adaptation of the acclaimed French series The Bureau.

***Which Egyptian goddess*** – often considered the daughter of Hathor and Ra and the consort of Thoth– was the personification of truth, order and justice, and would weigh the hearts of the dead against her feather? Those found unworthy were consumed by the goddess Ammit.
The moons of Uranus are either named after characters from Shakespeare or from ***which author’s*** poem The Rape of the Lock?
Released in 1985 and featuring the singles ‘Cloudbusting’ and ‘Running up That Hill’, ***what is the fifth studio album by Kate Bush***?
***How many players*** compete on the field for a rugby league team, compared to rugby union’s fifteen?

***Which membrane-bound organelle*** acts as the waste disposal system of an animal cell by digesting unwanted materials in the cytoplasm? This organelle can also destroy invading bacteria or viruses and can help a damaged cell self-destruct.
An important work in existential philosophy, Being and Time was written by ***which 20th century German philosopher***?
One of the best-selling albums of all time, Rumours was a 1977 release from ***which band***?
Mount Dena is the highest peak of ***which mountain range***, which stretches from southern Turkey across northern Iraq and into south-western Iran?
***Who became the first Japanese golfer*** to win a major golf tournament when he won the 2021 US Masters by just one stroke?
A popular side dish or dip from the Levant, baba ghanoush is primarily made from ***which culinary vegetable***, which is roasted, chopped or mashed, and mixed with oil, lemon juice and tahini?
***Which actor*** played the role of Cyril Blamire [BLAY-mire] in the first two series of the classic sitcom Last of The Summer Wine? His film career included roles in Patton and A Clockwork Orange.
Which English novelist’s early works were published under the pseudonym Boz and based on his periodical short stories Sketches by Boz?
***Which Austrian physicist*** gives his name to the apparent change of frequency in a sound wave perceived by an observer as the source of the sound passes?

In the 2007 film I’m Not There, six different actors portrayed different aspects of Bob Dylan’s life and career. The only female role amongst these six was that of Jude Quinn, who was played by ***which actress***?
***What is the name of the music festival*** that takes place annually during August in Budapest? The venue for the festival is a 108-hectare island on the Danube.
Voiced by Richard White, Gaston is the main antagonist of ***which 1991*** Disney film?
***Which stand-up comedian***, born Royston Vasey, uses the nickname ‘Chubby’? He is known for offensive comedy and a disdain for political correctness.
***Which lady-in-waiting to Catherine of Aragon*** became a mistress of Henry VIII [the eighth] and bore him Henry FitzRoy, the only illegitimate child king Henry acknowledged?
The hairy-nosed is an Asian species of ***which semiaquatic mammal*** that leaves a distinctive type of dung, known as spraints?
Not to be confused with portamento, ***what Italian term*** is used in music to refer to a glide between notes? It is notated by a wiggly line linking the beginning and end notes of the slide.
***What Greek dish*** is sometimes compared to lasagna, since both are layered, use minced meat and are topped with bechamel sauce? Unlike lasagna, this dish typically includes aubergine.
From 1986 to 1990, ***which actor*** played the role of Seymour Utterthwaite in Last of The Summer Wine? His TV career also included roles in Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Spy and Countdown to War.

***Who became the first English golfer*** to win the US Masters since Nick Faldo when he beat Jordan Spieth and Lee Westwood by three strokes to take the title in 2016? He failed to make the cut the following season and by 2018 he had dropped to 462nd in the world rankings?
One of the best-selling albums of all time, Bat Out of Hell was a 1977 release from ***which solo singer***?
explanation: Meat LOAF (or Michael Lee ADAY, Marvin Lee ADAY)

question: ***How many points*** are awarded for a try in a rugby league match, compared to the five awarded in rugby union?

***Which longtime companion of the later-George IV*** [the fourth] secretly contracted a marriage in 1785 to the then-Prince of Wales? The union was invalid under English law at the time as his father, George III [the third], had not consented to it.
explanation: Maria FITZHERBERT (accept Maria WELD, Maria SMYTHE)

question: The northern hairy-nosed and the southern hairy-nosed are two of the three species of ***which stocky, burrowing marsupials*** that leave distinctive cube-shaped dung?
Along with Spanish, ***which other European language*** has co-official status in the southern Argentinian province of Chubut?
The English novelist and poet Mary Ann Evans published her novels under ***what male pseudonym***?
***Who*** played the role of Alice in I’m Not There? She won an Oscar for playing a character with the same name in 2014’s Still Alice.

In January 2025, ***which Chinese AI company*** launched its first chatbot, which became the most downloaded app from the iOS App Store in the United States, and caused Nvidia’s share price to drop by 18%?
Susanna Hoffs was the lead singer of ***which all-female pop rock*** band who had a number 1 hit in the UK in 1989?
***What name*** is given to the Italian dish of veal shanks braised with white wine, stock and vegetables such as carrots, celery and onions?

The Resistance is a 2010 role-playing card-based social deduction party game in which players attempt to reveal the spy among them. ***What name***, after a mythical place, is given to the popular 2012 Arthurian-themed variant of the game?
***Who was the last Australian*** to win the men’s singles title at the Australian Open, doing so in 1976 to claim his only slam title?
***What UNESCO World Heritage Site in Delhi*** consists of a 13th-century stone minaret and victory tower constructed in the fortified city of Lal Kot?
The E-Type was a grand tourer model manufactured from 1961 to 1974 by ***which British car manufacturer***?
In ***which Roald Dahl book*** does the title character steal chickens, hams and cider night after night from the farmers Boggis, Bunce and Bean?

The civil rights organisation the NAACP was formed in 1909 partly in response to race riots the summer of the previous year in ***which state capital city***? This followed a similar event in Atlanta in 1906.

Famous instances of ***what specific type of relationship*** include Telly Savalas to Jennifer Aniston, Elton John to Brooklyn Beckham, and Steven Spielberg to both Drew Barrymore and Gwyneth Paltrow?
In 2024, ***which author*** released the highly-anticipated autobiographical work Knife: Meditations After an Attempted Murder, a recount of the stabbing he suffered at a public lecture in 2022?
